rationale: Both give reasonable engine lists with pros, cons, longevity notes and a goal-based recommendation table, and both correctly flag Unity WebGL as the main longevity risk. A is more accurate and better organized. It groups engines by 2D, 3D and cross-platform export, and correctly distinguishes Babylon.js as a full engine (physics, input, animation, Microsoft-backed) from Three.js and PixiJS as renderers. B lumps Babylon.js with Three.js as 'build everything yourself' and calls them free of any single corporate owner, which is wrong for Babylon. B also claims Construct's engine is now open-source, which is not the case. B's inclusion of Construct 3 for no-code prototyping is a useful addition. A has one factual slip (melonJS is not built on LimeJS). Overall A's characterizations are sounder and its longevity reasoning more reliable.
